subject: Post-call recap: Rate limits & overage pricing — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@acme.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.reai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Rate limits & overage pricing — next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the walkthrough of Acme's planned usage patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size pricing options correctly: 

Summary of what we heard
- Steady-state: ~350M tokens/month across inference features (summarization + classification).
- Peak bursts: up to ~12k RPS for short marketing spikes (10-20 minutes), historically 2-3x baseline QPS.
- Tolerance for brief throttling: low for user-facing flows; prefer graceful degradation.

Key open asks for sizing/pricing (can you confirm):
1) 30-day rolling max tokens and average daily peak minute (or sample logs).
2) Target budget range (monthly) so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated.
3) Ideal $/1M tokens you want to hit for long-term contract (you mentioned ~$900-1,200 / 1M tokens as a target on the call).

What I'll send next
- A short pricing comparison (hosted pay-as-you-go vs dedicated reserved capacity) with unit economics and overage tiers.
- Options for burst support and quota increase SLAs.
- A simple mutual action plan if you want us to propose a pilot.

Attachments: redwood_rate_limits_v1.pdf (rate-limit patterns & overage examples) — sharing preliminary reference.

Next step: can you share the 30-day rolling max and a rough monthly budget range? Would also be helpful to have Sara on any follow-ups for procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

From: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:20:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Rate limits & overage pricing — next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers: 
- We can pull the 30-day rolling max and should have a CSV by end of day tomorrow; rough ballpark: 300-380M tokens/month.
- Budget: initially $75k-120k/mo for hosted + overages, with potential to move to dedicated if unit economics are below our target.
- On $/1M tokens: yes, target is in the ~$900 range for committed pricing.

Questions: 
1) How does Redwood handle bursts beyond quota today? Is there an automatic overage charge or do you soft-throttle?
2) If we need a quota increase for a campaign, what's the lead time (hours/days)?

I'm attaching our rough monthly forecast (acme_monthly_forecast.xlsx).

— Mike
Mike Johnson
Head of Product Operations, Acme Corp
mike.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.reai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Rate limits & overage pricing — next steps

Thanks Mike — got the high-level numbers, that's helpful. Below is a practical breakdown so you can evaluate versus your $/1M target. Rafael added a short note on technical options below.

Pricing (illustrative, USD) — hosted (pay-as-you-go):
- Base rate: $1,200 / 1M tokens for first 100M tokens/month.
- Tiered overage: $1,050 / 1M for next 200M; $950 / 1M beyond that.
- Burst surcharge: short bursts (<=30min) that exceed quota are billed at a 1.25x multiplier on the applicable tier; we do not automatically hard-throttle unless you opt into that behavior.

Dedicated (reserved capacity) — example economics:
- 3-month reserved commit: effective $700-850 / 1M (depends on model mix & utilization).
- Includes burst window configurable up to 2x committed throughput for limited minutes per day (pre-approved).

Quota increase & SLA options:
- Standard: manual quota increase request (same business day for <2x increases if requested before 2pm PT; otherwise next business day).
- Fast-track: pre-approved burst policy + billing authorization lets us auto-increase quotas up to 2x for short windows (minutes-hours). This requires a short addendum (SLA exception) and a billing pre-authorization.

Recommendations based on Acme's profile:
- If you plan to stay in the ~$300-380M token range, a reserved commit (6-12 months) will likely meet your $/1M target.
- For going-live with marketing spikes, enable the fast-track burst policy for critical routes to avoid user impact; we can cap non-critical flows to soft-throttle.

Next steps (proposed)
1) We'll run a quick unit-economics model on your attached forecast and share a 2-option quote (hosted vs 12mo reserved).
2) Rafael to validate burst configuration & provide recommended soft/hard throttle settings.
3) If you want auto-burst, we'll prepare a short SLA addendum and DocuSign link.

Attachments: redwood_rate_limits_v1.pdf (detailed examples), link to HubSpot record.

Thanks,
Marissa

-----
Note from Rafael (cc):
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Rate limits & overage pricing — technical note

Quick technical note: if Acme wants auto-burst up to 2x, we recommend:
- Configure prefix-based caching for user-facing generative endpoints to reduce token volume during peaks.
- Set a 1-minute burst window with exponential backoff for non-critical endpoints.
- Pre-authorize billing for burst capacity and set alert hooks to notify both teams at 80%/100% thresholds.

I'll send a sample quota config and a snippet of recommended rate-limit headers you can use. — Rafael

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.reai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sample quota config & burst behavior

Mike — following up with the sample config we discussed:

- Default monthly quota: 350M tokens (example).
- Auto-burst policy: allow up to 2x peak throughput for windows up to 30 minutes when billing pre-auth is enabled.
- Soft-throttle: 90% of quota => inject 429 warnings with Retry-After header set to progressive backoff.
- Hard-throttle: >2x sustained >30 minutes => enforced 503 fallback to lower-tier model.

Operational notes:
- Quota increase lead time: same business day for <2x if asked before 2pm PT; emergency increases require a signed SLA addendum and take ~2 hours to provision during business hours.
- We can pre-authorize a one-off burst allowance for your planned campaigns; would need Sara's procurement sign-off.

Attachment: acme_rate_limit_config_example.json (sample config) — attaching as part of thread.

— Rafael

From: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Rate limits & overage pricing — next steps

Appreciate the detail — this is very helpful. I'll review the numbers with Sara and procurement and get back to you with our preferred path (likely a 6-12mo reserved commit with a fast-track burst add-on). Will aim to respond by Friday EOD.

Thanks,
Mike
